paragraphs: Brothers, do not be afraid of men’s sin. Love a person even in his sin, for that is the likeness of God’s own love and the highest love on earth. Love all of God’s creation, the whole of it and every grain of sand in it. Love every leaf, every ray of God’s light. Love the animals, love the plants, love everything. If you love everything, you will see the divine mystery in things. Once you see it, you will understand it better every day. And in the end you will love the whole world with a love that takes in everything. Love the animals: God gave them the beginnings of thought and an untroubled joy. Do not disturb it. Do not torment them, do not take their happiness from them, do not work against God’s intention. Man, do not boast of being above the animals. They are without sin, and you, for all your greatness, defile the earth by appearing on it, and you leave the traces of your foulness behind you. Alas, that is true of almost every one of us! Love children above all, for they too are sinless, like the angels. They live to soften and purify our hearts, and in a way to guide us. Woe to anyone who offends a child! Father Anfim taught me to love children. That kind, silent man often spent the farthings people gave us on our wanderings on sweets and cakes for the children. He could not pass a child without being moved. That is the kind of man he was.

Some thoughts leave one perplexed, especially at the sight of men’s sin, and one wonders whether to use force or humble love. Always decide on humble love. If you make that decision once and for all, you can conquer the whole world. Loving humility is wonderfully strong. It is the strongest thing there is, and nothing else is like it.

Every day, every hour, every minute, walk around yourself and watch yourself, and see that the picture you present is a decent one. You pass a little child, and you pass by spiteful, with ugly words, with an angry heart. You may not have noticed the child, but he has seen you, and your image, ugly and ignoble, may stay in his defenseless heart. You do not know it, but you may have planted an evil seed in him, and it may grow. All of that because you were not careful in front of the child, because you did not cultivate in yourself a careful, actively kind love. Brothers, love is a teacher, but one must know how to acquire it. It is hard to acquire, it is bought dearly, it is won slowly by long labor. For we must love not just now and then, for a moment, but forever. Anyone can love now and then, even the wicked can.

My brother asked the birds to forgive him. That sounds senseless, but it is right, for everything is like an ocean, everything flows and blends together. A touch in one place sets off a movement at the other end of the earth. It may be senseless to ask the birds’ forgiveness, but the birds would be happier at your side, a little happier at least, and so would children and all the animals, if you were nobler than you are now. It is all like an ocean, I tell you. Then you would pray to the birds too, consumed by a love that embraces everything, in a kind of rapture, and ask them to forgive your sin as well. Treasure this ecstasy, however senseless it may seem to men.

My friends, pray to God for gladness. Be glad like children, like the birds of heaven. And do not let men’s sin confuse you in what you do. Do not fear that it will wear down your work and stop it from being finished. Do not say, “Sin is mighty, wickedness is mighty, our evil surroundings are mighty, and we are alone and helpless, and our evil surroundings are wearing us down and keeping our good work from being done.” Run from that despondency, children! There is only one means of salvation: take it on yourself and make yourself responsible for all men’s sins. That is the truth, you know, friends, for as soon as you honestly make yourself responsible for everything and for everyone, you will see at once that it really is so, and that you are to blame for every person and for all things. But if you throw your own laziness and weakness onto others, you will end by sharing the pride of Satan and grumbling against God.

Of the pride of Satan, this is what I think: it is hard for us on earth to understand it, and so it is easy to fall into error and share in it, even imagining that we are doing something grand and fine. Indeed, there are many of the strongest feelings and movements of our nature that we cannot understand on earth. Do not let that be a stumbling block, and do not think it can serve as an excuse for anything you do. For the Eternal Judge asks of you what you can understand, not what you cannot. You will know that yourself afterward, for then you will see all things truly and will not dispute them. Here on earth we are, in a way, lost, and if it were not for the precious image of Christ before us, we would be undone and altogether lost, like the human race before the flood. Much on earth is hidden from us, but to make up for that we have been given a precious, mysterious sense of our living bond with the other world, with the higher world of heaven. The roots of our thoughts and feelings are not here but in other worlds. That is why the philosophers say that we cannot grasp the reality of things on earth.

God took seeds from different worlds and sowed them on this earth, and His garden grew, and everything came up that could come up. But whatever grows lives and is alive only through its feeling of contact with other, mysterious worlds. If that feeling grows weak in you or is destroyed, the heavenly growth in you will die away. Then you will be indifferent to life and even come to hate it. That is what I think.
_(h) Can a Man judge his Fellow Creatures? Faith to the End_

Remember above all that you cannot be a judge of anyone. For no one can judge a criminal until he recognizes that he is just such a criminal as the man standing before him, and that he may be more to blame than anyone for that crime. When he understands that, he will be able to be a judge. Though that sounds absurd, it is true. If I had been righteous myself, perhaps there would have been no criminal standing before me. If you can take on yourself the crime of the criminal your heart is judging, take it at once, suffer for him yourself, and let him go without reproach. And even if the law itself makes you his judge, act in the same spirit as far as you can, for he will go away and condemn himself more bitterly than you have done. If, after your kiss, he goes away unmoved, mocking you, do not let that be a stumbling block to you. It shows that his time has not yet come, but it will come in due course. And if it does not come, no matter. If not he, then someone else in his place will understand and suffer, and judge and condemn himself, and the truth will be fulfilled. Believe that, believe it without doubt, for in that lies all the hope and faith of the saints.

Work without ceasing. If you remember at night as you go to sleep, “I have not done what I ought to have done,” get up at once and do it. If the people around you are spiteful and callous and will not listen to you, fall down before them and beg their forgiveness, for in truth you are to blame for their not wanting to listen. And if you cannot speak to them in their bitterness, serve them in silence and in humility, never losing hope. If all men abandon you and even drive you away by force, then when you are left alone, fall on the earth and kiss it, water it with your tears, and it will bring forth fruit, even though no one has seen or heard you in your solitude. Believe to the end, even if all men went astray and you were left the only one faithful. Bring your offering even then and praise God in your loneliness. And if two of you are gathered together, then there is a whole world, a world of living love. Embrace each other tenderly and praise God, for His truth has been fulfilled, if only in the two of you.

If you sin yourself, and grieve even to death over your sins or over a sudden sin, then rejoice for others. Rejoice for the righteous man. Rejoice that if you have sinned, he is righteous and has not sinned.

If the evil-doing of men moves you to indignation and overwhelming distress, even to a desire for vengeance on the evil-doers, shun that feeling above all things. Go at once and seek suffering for yourself, as though you yourself were guilty of that wrong. Accept that suffering and bear it, and your heart will find comfort. You will understand that you too are guilty, for you might have been a light to the evil-doers, even as the one sinless man, and you were not a light to them. If you had been a light, you would have lit the path for others too, and the evil-doer might have been saved from his sin by your light. And even if your light was shining and you see that men were not saved by it, hold firm and do not doubt the power of the heavenly light. Believe that if they were not saved, they will be saved later. And if they are not saved later, then their sons will be saved, for your light will not die even when you are dead. The righteous man departs, but his light remains. Men are always saved after the death of the deliverer. Men reject their prophets and kill them, but they love their martyrs and honor those whom they have killed. You are working for the whole, you are acting for the future. Seek no reward, for your reward on this earth is great: the spiritual joy that is granted only to the righteous man. Do not fear the great or the mighty, but be wise and always serene. Know the measure, know the times, study that. When you are left alone, pray. Love to throw yourself on the earth and kiss it. Kiss the earth and love it with an unceasing, consuming love. Love all men, love everything. Seek that rapture and ecstasy. Water the earth with the tears of your joy and love those tears. Do not be ashamed of that ecstasy. Prize it, for it is a gift of God and a great one. It is not given to many, but only to the elect.
_(i) Of Hell and Hell Fire, a Mystic Reflection_

Fathers and teachers, I ask myself, “What is hell?” I maintain that it is the suffering of being unable to love. Once, in infinite existence, immeasurable in time and space, a spiritual creature was given, on his coming to earth, the power to say, “I am and I love.” Once, only once, he was given a moment of active, _living_ love, and for that earthly life was given him, and with it times and seasons. And that happy creature rejected the priceless gift. He did not prize it or love it, he scorned it and stayed callous. Such a one, having left the earth, sees Abraham’s bosom and talks with Abraham, as we are told in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus. He sees heaven and can go up to the Lord. But that is just his torment: to rise up to the Lord without ever having loved, to be brought close to those who have loved when he despised their love. For he sees clearly and says to himself, “Now I understand, and though I now thirst to love, there will be nothing great in my love, no sacrifice, for my earthly life is over. Abraham will not come, even with a drop of living water (that is the gift of earthly active life) to cool the fiery thirst for spiritual love that burns in me now, though I despised it on earth. There is no more life for me and there will be no more time! Even though I would gladly give my life for others, it can never be, for that life which could be sacrificed for love is past, and now there is a gulf fixed between that life and this existence.”

They talk of hell fire in the material sense. I do not go into that mystery and I shun it. But I think that if there were fire in the material sense, they would be glad of it, for I imagine that in bodily agony their far greater spiritual agony would be forgotten for a moment. Besides, that spiritual agony cannot be taken from them, for that suffering is not outside them but within them. And if it could be taken from them, I think it would be even more bitter for the unhappy creatures. For even if the righteous in Paradise forgave them, seeing their torments, and called them up to heaven in their infinite love, they would only multiply their torments, for they would awaken in them an even keener, flaming thirst for responsive, active and grateful love, which is now impossible. In the timidity of my heart, however, I imagine that the very recognition of this impossibility would serve at last to console them. For by accepting the love of the righteous together with the impossibility of repaying it, by this submissiveness and the effect of this humility, they will attain at last a certain likeness of that active love which they scorned in life, something like its outward expression.... I am sorry, friends and brothers, that I cannot express this clearly. But woe to those who have killed themselves on earth, woe to the suicides! I believe that there can be none more miserable than they. They tell us that it is a sin to pray for them, and outwardly the Church, as it were, renounces them, but in my secret heart I believe that we may pray even for them. Love can never be an offense to Christ. For such as those I have prayed inwardly all my life, I admit it, fathers and teachers, and even now I pray for them every day.

Oh, there are some who stay proud and fierce even in hell, in spite of their certain knowledge and sight of the absolute truth. There are some fearful ones who have given themselves over entirely to Satan and his proud spirit. For such as these, hell is voluntary and ever consuming. They are tortured by their own choice. For they have cursed themselves, cursing God and life. They live on their vindictive pride like a starving man in the desert sucking blood out of his own body. But they are never satisfied, and they refuse forgiveness, they curse God who calls them. They cannot look on the living God without hatred, and they cry out that the God of life should be annihilated, that God should destroy Himself and His own creation. And they will burn in the fire of their own wrath forever and yearn for death and annihilation. But they will not reach death....

Here the manuscript of Alexey Fyodorovitch Karamazov ends. I repeat, it is incomplete and fragmentary. The biographical details, for instance, cover only Father Zossima’s earliest youth. Of his teaching and opinions, we find sayings brought together that were evidently spoken on very different occasions. His words during the last few hours have not been kept separate from the rest, but their general character can be gathered from what we have in Alexey Fyodorovitch’s manuscript.

The elder’s death came in the end quite unexpectedly. Those gathered around him that last evening realized that his death was approaching, yet it was hard to imagine that it would come so suddenly. On the contrary, his friends, as I mentioned already, saw him that night so cheerful and talkative that they were convinced there was at least a temporary change for the better in his condition. Even five minutes before his death, they said afterwards in wonder, it was impossible to foresee it. He seemed suddenly to feel a sharp pain in his chest. He turned pale and pressed his hands to his heart. All rose from their seats and hurried to him. But though he was suffering, he still looked at them with a smile. He sank slowly from his chair to his knees, then bowed his face to the ground, stretched out his arms, and as though in joyful ecstasy, praying and kissing the ground, he quietly and joyfully gave up his soul to God.

The news of his death spread at once through the hermitage and reached the monastery. The dead man’s closest friends, and those whose position made it their duty, began to prepare the body according to the ancient ritual, and all the monks gathered in the church. Before dawn the news of the death reached the town. By morning the whole town was talking of the event, and crowds were streaming from the town to the monastery. But this subject will be treated in the next book. I will only add here that before a day had passed, something happened so unexpected, so strange, so upsetting and bewildering in its effect on the monks and the townspeople, that after all these years that day of general suspense is still vividly remembered in the town.
